name: Junia (relative of Paul)
title: Prominent Apostle
summary: Junia was a Jewish woman who, together with Andronicus, was a relative of the apostle Paul. They were Christians before Paul and were highly regarded among the apostles. Both had been imprisoned alongside Paul for their faith.

keyEvents.title: Greeting from Paul
keyEvents.description: Paul sends greetings to Junia and Andronicus in his letter to the church in Rome, referring to them as prominent among the apostles.

keyEvents.title: Early Christians
keyEvents.description: Junia and Andronicus were Christians before Paul himself was converted, meaning they were among the very first believers.

keyEvents.title: Fellow Prisoners with Paul
keyEvents.description: Junia and Andronicus had been imprisoned together with Paul, likely because of their preaching of the gospel.

keyEvents.title: Recognized Among the Apostles
keyEvents.description: Paul describes Junia and Andronicus as highly regarded among the apostles, indicating their significant role in the early church.
